newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-German July industry output rose 0.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-German July industry output rose 0.2 pct.

text.p: German industrial output rose 0.2 percent in July from the previous month, the fifth monthly rise in a row, but slowing from 0.7 percent growth in June, the economics ministry said on Tuesday.
Output was down 1.6 percent from July 1995, compared with a 0.8 percent year-on-year decline in June, according to Reuters calculations based on Bundesbank statistics.

"It is close to consensus, and the fifth monthly rise in a row which is unusual and does confirm that the economy is in a nice uptrend," said economist Holger Schmieding at Merrill Lynch in Frankfurt.

"July was 0.9 percent over the average of the second quarter. If output remains only steady from now on, it will give quite reasonable third quarter GDP growth. "West German industry is doing well which fits in with the latest, very strong, Ifo report for July." (Ifo is one of Germany's respected economic institutes.)
Average market expectations had been for slightly stronger figures, a 0.4 percent rise in output from the previous month, and a 1.3 percent decline from the year-earlier month.
Norbert Braems of Barclays de Zoete Wedd in Frankfurt found the July numbers disappointing, based on expectations stemming in part from the same Ifo report.
"We believed the numbers should be higher, after the Ifo institute said July numbers should be better. The car sector was strong in July.
"These data are preliminary, and there may be some revisions. Particularly east Germany looks not very good. Ifo was very strong on the current production level."
The ministry said that summer holidays make the data volatile in short-term comparison.
The consumer goods sector saw the biggest retreat, with output declining 3.9 percent. A 4.2 percent rebound in the construction sector was not enough to make up the difference.

Output in west Germany rose 0.5 percent from the previous month but was down 1.7 percent from the year-earlier month, while east German output declined 5.5 percent from June and rose 3.7 percent from July 1995.
